newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Astra again focus of rumours.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Astra again focus of rumours.

text.p: Indonesia's largest vehicle manufacturer Astra International was again in focus on the Jakarta stock market on Monday after reports that a group linked to President Suharto could make a general offer, brokers said.

The share surged in early trade to 4,150 rupiah ($1.80) before easing to 3,925 rupiah, down 25, by the close with 7.4 million shares changing hands. The trading volume was the second highest on the board.
Brokers ascribed the early surge to a report in Bisnis Indonesia newspaper which quoted one shareholder as saying that a price of 4,200 rupiah per share was a reasonable valuation of the company.
Other newspapers said it was possible that the Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto, could make a general offer for Astra shares.
Nusamba is headed by timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, who owns 10 percent of the group with the remainder held by Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.
Hasan was not available for comment. Antara news agency said he was in Nusa Tenggara province as part of a delegation accompanying Suharto on a tour.
Bisnis Indonesia quoted businessman Sofjan Wanandi as saying that 4,200 rupiah per share was a fair valuation for Astra.
But Wanandi stressed that his Gemala Group had not been approached for its stake in the company. Gemala owns about 20 million Astra shares, or about two percent.
"That news led to active local buying in early trade but it failed to reach the price of 4,200 rupiah. Some profit-taking later surfaced," said one foreign broker.

Other brokers said they had heard that a consortium comprising Hasan, tobacco magnate Putera Sampoerna and Suharto's daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana was preparing to make a general offer for Astra shares.
"We heard that they are planning to submit the proposal to Stock Exchange Supervisory Agency perhaps this week," said a broker from a major local firm.
Sampoerna, the head of cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, already effectively controls the largest stake in Astra.
He owns 9.81 percent of the company in his own right while a subsidiary of PT Sampoerna has said it has bought 2.85 percent.
Hasan said in a newspaper interview last week that Nusamba did not yet own any shares in Astra but would like to. That report led to a surge in Astra's price on Friday.
Rukmana, who controls toll-road operator PT Citra Marga, has also been previously linked by newspapers to Astra but her office has declined to comment.
A spokesman for the supervisory agency said he had received no word that such an offer was imminent.
